week.short: Light Rain then Rain And Snow
week.detailed: Rain between 8am and 5pm, then rain and snow. Cloudy. High near 50, with temperatures falling to around 43 in the afternoon. Northeast wind 3 to 9 mph. Chance of precipitation is 100%. New rainfall amounts between a half and three quarters of an inch possible.

nws_alerts.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 16 at 10:01PM MST until November 18 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
nws_alerts.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. For the Wasatch Mountains, forecast snow
totals of 4 to 8 inches above 8000 feet with locally higher amounts
in excess of 12 inches for the Upper Cottonwoods. For the Wasatch
Back, 1 to 4 inches with the highest amounts for Park City and the
Ogden valley.

* WHERE...The Wasatch Mountains, and Wasatch Back.

* WHEN...From 11 AM Tuesday to 11 AM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult at times along mountain routes.
The hazardous conditions will impact the Tuesday evening and
Wednesday morning commutes on higher passes such as Parleys Summit.

nws_alerts.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 17 at 12:42AM MST until November 18 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Pocatello ID
nws_alerts.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 2 and 8
inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Bear River Range.

* WHEN...From 11 AM this morning to 5 AM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. Gusty winds could bring
down tree branches.

discussion.key_messages: - There is a marginal risk for excessive rainfall (level 1 of 4) across southern Utah today, as a strong cold front sweeps through the region. - Winter Weather Advisories are in effect for the Wasatch, western Uinta, and southern mountains where 4 to 10 inches of snow is expected through tonight. A Winter Weather Advisory is also in effect for the Wasatch Back, where 1 to 4 inches of snow is expected. - Another storm system will bring significant mountain snow Thursday into Friday, with snow levels falling near to below 5000 feet by Friday. Another 6 to 12 inches of mountain snow, with locally higher amounts near 2 feet for the upper Cottonwoods and near Brian Head can be expected. - Freezing temperatures are increasing in probability for the Virgin River corridor near Zion National Park Saturday and Sunday mornings
